THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173 (1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 07.05.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.314/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL AND PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE,
HAVERI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The claim petition is filed seeking enhancement of compensation by the mother of deceased.
The deceased was admittedly a bachelor.
He was a police constable and Rs.17,484/- was the monthly income.

The Tribunal has not awarded future prospects though the deceased was aged 28 years and instead of applying multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased, the Tribunal has taken the age of the mother into consideration.
Now the law is well settled that age of the deceased is to be taken into consideration while choosing the multiplier.
Since the deceased was 28 years, 40% is to be added towards future prospects.
2. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that contribution made by deceased towards provident fund, pension and insurance have to be deducted while calculating the income.

The position of law in this regard is well settled in terms of judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Vimal Kanwar and Others Vs. Kishore Dan and Others [ACJ 2013 3 1441] and no such deduction is permissible.

entities.text: Vimal Kanwar and Others Vs. Kishore Dan and Others [ACJ 2013 3 1441]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Under the circumstance, the compensation payable under the head loss of dependency would be:
Rs.17,484, - Rs.200 professional tax = Rs.17,284 + 50% future prospects =
Rs.25,926/-
Rs.25,926 x 12 x 17 x 50%= Rs.26,44,452/-
3.
The appellant is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expense and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.

4. In all, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.27,14,452/- with interest at 6% p.a.
5.

Learned counsel for respondent - insurer has filed an affidavit said to have been filed by appellant in this case and in the said affidavit it is stated that if compensation awarded by the Tribunal is paid Smt. Dyamavva W/O. Hanumappa ... vs Sri. Basanagouda S/O Shankaragouda ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151441545/
2
by the insurer, the appellant would not file any appeal against the judgment and award.
6. This Court has perused the affidavit.

Merely because an affidavit is filed, wherein the appellant stated that she is not going to file appeal in the event of insurer satisfying the award, it cannot be said that the right of the appellant to claim higher compensation is taken away.
Even in the absence of that affidavit the insurer was under obligation to discharge the award passed against the insurer.
The payment is not made because of the affidavit.

It can be noticed that the claimant was aged 52 years and she is an illiterate and given the fact that she has lost her son it is quite possible that she was under stress and was wanted to avoid further litigation and might have executed an affidavit stating that she is not going to file appeal.

That cannot operate as an estoppel given the fact that the insurer has not made out any ground to prove that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side and as already noticed the liability is not based on affidavit.
The liability is statutory liability governed by policy of insurance.
Under the circumstance, the affidavit filed does not come in the way of appellant seeking enhancement.
7. Respondent - insurer shall deposit the compensation before the Tribunal within six weeks from today.
8. Appeal is allowed in part and the judgment and award of the Tribunal are modified as indicated above.
9. Appellant is not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 587 days in filing the appeal.
